key_insight: ProCARE turns real-world study automation into a constrained compilation problem by grounding LLM workflows in dataset-specific evidence contracts and a typed intermediate representation.
clinical_relevance: It could make automated observational analyses from EHR and claims data more reliable by reducing schema mismatches, temporal mistakes, and unsupported clinical interpretations.
method: Builds profile-derived Evidence Contracts that describe variables, time attributes, distributions, and evidentiary limits.
Compiles study goals into RWS-IR, a strongly typed format for variables, time relations, analysis units, and statistical tasks.
Uses deterministic validation and localized repair to fix issues across schema mapping, cohort building, derivation, analysis, and interpretation.
evidence_signal: On 36 EHR-based benchmark tasks, ProCARE outperformed strong LLM-agent baselines in executability, semantic consistency, and traceable conclusions, with automated violation diagnoses moderately to substantially matching blinded expert review.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate dataset profiling and may still require careful human oversight when clinical semantics are incomplete or ambiguous.
paper_title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts
